title: Tweening a Color instance shader parameter throws a type mismatch
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Fedora 41, Linux 6.13.9, Wayland, RX6600, i7-12700KF

### Issue description

When a shader has a Color-type instance parameter, leaving it on the default value crashes a tween that tries to tween it to something else with:

```
E 0:00:00:175   cube.gd:5 @ _ready(): Type mismatch between initial and final value: Nil and Color
  <C++ Error>   Method/function failed. Returning: false
  <C++ Source>  scene/animation/tween.cpp:86 @ _validate_type_match()
  <Stack Trace> cube.gd:5 @ _ready()
```

using the code:
```
tween.tween_property(self, "instance_shader_parameters/Color", Color.BLUE_VIOLET, 0.5)
```

This problem could be more general than this, but this is where I encountered it.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a mesh instance, set it to some built-in mesh (box works for me)
- Set its material override to a new ShaderMaterial
- Set the shader to a new visual shader
- In the shader, create a ColorParameter (I named mine `Color`), assign it to albedo and set it to Instance qualifier
- Enable and set its default color (to anything)
- Attach a script to the mesh instance:
```gdscript
extends MeshInstance3D

func _ready() -> void:
	var tween = get_tree().create_tween()
	tween.tween_property(self, "instance_shader_parameters/Color", Color.BLUE_VIOLET, 0.5)

``` 
- Run the scene

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[TweenBug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19726757/TweenBug.zip)
